title: 火炎 (Kaen / FIRE)
why: The black mass of the figure arched backward against a flat orange-red field, with only the cyan-white flame head as a cool accent, is the whole silhouette-first idea the ending pose was built from, and the dangling orange straps echo the lich's trailing limbs.

title: 奇麗 (Kirei)
why: A violet smoke plume erupts from the top of a back-tilted head, eyes covered, against flat saturated yellow: Kaen's 'element crowns the head on a colour field' idea with a complementary pair, and the cream clothing sits close to bone-cream.

title: Q
why: A head tipped down on a bent neck, a flat yellow halo ring and glowing yellow eyes on a black-painted figure against neutral grey: a one-colour accent doing all the work.

title: HALF
why: A gold-plated rib cage and spine is the only bright mass on a black tee against a flat blue-grey, so a skeleton reads instantly as a graphic emblem rather than as horror.

title: 強火 (Tsuyobi)
why: One clawed hand with a flame at each fingertip, blue-white to orange, on deep red: a hand-only composition that reads at thumbnail size and rhymes with the bronze Sabazios hand.

title: 蛇姫様 (Hebihime, 'Snake Princess')
why: A tiny gold-clad figure at the foot of a vast heap of crumpled gold under a black storm sky, with a vertical kanji title: a scale contrast and a gold-on-black palette that fits a serpent-and-treasure theme.

title: 孔雀 (Kujaku, 'Peacock')
why: Glossy black gloves with bone-like ridges clasp a bare torso in smoky blue-teal light, with the title as two white vertical kanji at lower right: skeleton hands, gloss and glow in one image.

title: 犬姫 (Inuhime)
why: A figure in pale green court robes kneels in a near-black teal field with the two-kanji title in metallic gold at lower left, a clean model for gold lettering that sits in the dark instead of on a plate.

title: Island Life
credits: Jean-Paul Goude (cover image, a montage; per en.wikipedia 'Island Life')
why: A single body bent into an impossible arabesque against a flat pale-blue room reads as one clean silhouette, the nearest cousin to an arched-back, limbs-flung lich.

title: Vulnicura
credits: Artwork design M/M (Paris); cover photograph Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin (per en.wikipedia 'Vulnicura')
why: A figure in black latex with arms thrown open and a radiating spiked crown for a head sits against a near-white to yellow gradient, so silhouette and head-element survive at thumbnail size.

title: KiCk i
credits: Cover image by Arca, Carlos Sáez and Carlota Guerrero (per en.wikipedia 'KiCk i')
why: One small figure with mechanical limbs stands in a vast pale grey field, showing how much empty flat colour a single body can hold and where a logo could live.

title: Aladdin Sane
credits: Photograph by Brian Duffy (per en.wikipedia 'Aladdin Sane')
why: One bold painted mark across a closed-eyed face against a near-white field, plus a single teardrop, gives a cover a whole identity out of a single graphic gesture.

title: Heaven to a Tortured Mind
why: A crouched figure dissolving into streaks of white light on black shows how a body can be half-erased by a light source, the dark-field counterpart to the shaft of sun on the egg.

title: Homogenic
credits: Art direction Alexander McQueen; photography Nick Knight; sleeve design Me Company (per en.wikipedia 'Homogenic')
why: A symmetric figure whose head is crowned by a black sculptural form over a white-and-red robe on a pale blue gradient: a head-element and a strong shape-colour split in a centred portrait.

title: KICK BACK (Chainsaw Man opening)
why: A chainsaw-headed figure hauling a pull-cord against a flat saturated red, with the lettering as a distressed band across the top: head replaced by an object, one colour field, bold lettering.

title: Inferno (Fire Force opening)
why: A single orange flame emblem centred on pure black with a condensed white wordmark is the minimal icon-on-black version of the same idea, readable at a few pixels.

title: 紅蓮の弓矢 (Guren no Yumiya, Attack on Titan opening)
why: A gold-line crest on dark brown with no figure at all shows a game logo can be a heraldic emblem with lettering built into its geometry.

title: 廻廻奇譚 / 蒼のワルツ (Kaikai Kitan, Jujutsu Kaisen opening)
credits: Regular-edition jacket illustration by Mah (per ja.wikipedia, citing Natalie)
why: Black ink washes pooling around pale hands on a pure white field, with almost no colour, is a model for a monochrome capsule that lets one dark gesture carry the image.

title: 怪物 (Kaibutsu, BEASTARS season 2 opening)
why: Red-on-black wolf silhouettes between bare tree trunks with a thin vertical title: a two-tone, high-contrast figure that works as a pure silhouette.

title: Closer
credits: Design by Martyn Atkins and Peter Saville; photograph of the Appiani family tomb (Staglieno, Genoa) by Bernard Pierre Wolff, 1978 (per en.wikipedia 'Closer')
why: A found photograph of a mourning tomb sculpture inside a thin frame on a huge white field, with the title in tiny small caps: death handled with restraint and white space.

title: Oxygène
why: A skull exposed under the torn crust of a planet inside a blue glow gives bone a cosmic scale, and the painted surface is one the lich's cave art could imitate.

title: In Utero
credits: Robert Fisher (art direction, design) with Kurt Cobain (per en.wikipedia 'In Utero')
why: A transparent anatomical figure with feathered wings centred on cream cracked parchment shows a body read as anatomy and as angel at once, with the title in plain small type.

title: Grateful Dead (Skull & Roses)
credits: Alton Kelley and Stanley Mouse, from an illustration by Edmund J. Sullivan for the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam (per en.wikipedia)
why: A Victorian engraving of a skeleton crowned with roses reused inside a flat-colour poster frame with hand-drawn lettering: a direct precedent for reusing an old engraving of the dead.

title: Filosofem
credits: Theodor Kittelsen (painting 'Op under Fjeldet toner en Lur'; per en.wikipedia 'Filosofem')
why: A century-old painting of a lone cloaked figure blowing a horn beside a boulder in a pale misty valley, with a blackletter title, shows an old painting plus type can be a whole cover.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
credits: Storm Thorgerson (concept); design Hipgnosis and George Hardie (per en.wikipedia)
why: A single thin beam of white light enters a prism on pure black and leaves as a spectrum: the light-in-darkness and the prism in one shape, with no lettering at all.

title: The Serpent's Egg
credits: Sleeve design Brendan Perry and Vaughan Oliver (per en.wikipedia 'The Serpent's Egg')
why: A serpentine river seen from above in olive and ochre, with the title in a thin serif at lower right, makes the snake and the egg a landscape rather than an object.

title: It's Blitz!
credits: Urs Fischer (art direction, cover photography); art direction Karen O and Seb Marling (per en.wikipedia 'It's Blitz!')
why: A fist crushing an egg, yolk and shell caught mid-burst against flat white, makes the egg a thing that can be hurt, and the hand-and-egg pairing is the cleanest possible thumbnail.

title: Titanic Rising
credits: Brett Stanley (photography, set builds); Elijah Funk (layout) (per en.wikipedia 'Titanic Rising')
why: A bedroom sunk in deep blue water with bright light streaming down from the surface into the room, one small figure at the desk, is a close match for sunlight falling through a hole into a dark space.

title: Brotherhood of the Snake
why: Two pale vipers with fangs bared rise side by side over a burnt-orange ground, giving a ready-made composition for snakes approaching from the foreground.

title: Meliora
why: Long rays of light radiate from the top of the frame through a dark gothic hall, with a gold wordmark at the apex: light fanning down through darkness in a symmetrical layout.

title: Return of the Obra Dinn (Original Game Soundtrack)
why: A dithered 1-bit title in heavy blackletter over a dithered moon and ship, in two tones, shows lettering that looks native to a low-res pixel-dithered game.

title: Darkest Dungeon (Original Video Game Soundtrack, Deluxe Edition)
why: A jagged condensed serif title flanked by a small ornament on a black-and-red silhouette landscape is a game logo whose letterforms carry the mood by themselves.

title: 唱 (Show)
credits: Jacket illustration by ヤスタツ (Yasutatsu) (per ja.wikipedia 唱 (Adoの曲), citing Tower Records)
why: Huge gold kanji woven between the figures inside an ornate frame show a title that is part of the picture's structure rather than laid over it.

title: Habit
why: An ornate, spiky title in a muted engraved style over a scratchy line illustration on dusty pink is a model for lettering that shares the drawing's linework.

title: 無罪モラトリアム (Muzai Moratorium)
credits: Jacket design by art director 木村豊 (Yutaka Kimura) (per ja.wikipedia 無罪モラトリアム, citing Da Vinci News)
why: A hand-brushed kanji banner held up inside a press scrum makes the title a physical object in the scene, with the artist's name set small and sideways at the edge.
